module_title: Input and Output Devices - Foundational Basics
introduction: Input and Output (I/O) devices form one of the easiest and most scoring topics in competitive exams (SSC, Railways, Bank Clerk). At this foundational level, we will classify the basic hardware components used to feed data into the computer (Input) and retrieve processed results from it (Output).

core_concepts.title: Input Devices
core_concepts.description:
These are hardware devices used to enter raw data and instructions into the computer. Simply put, they send information 'IN' to the system. 
Examples: Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, Microphone (Mic), and Joystick.

core_concepts.title: Output Devices
core_concepts.description:
These are hardware devices that display, project, or physically reproduce the processed data (results) for the user. Simply put, they bring information 'OUT' of the system. 
Examples: Monitor (Screen), Printer, Speaker, and Projector.

core_concepts.title: Keyboard and Mouse (Primary Inputs)
core_concepts.description: The keyboard is the most common text-entry device (typically using the QWERTY layout). The mouse is a standard 'Pointing Device' invented by Douglas Engelbart, used to interact with the graphical user interface.

core_concepts.title: Monitor and Printer (Primary Outputs)
core_concepts.description: A monitor provides a 'Soft Copy' output (a temporary visual display on a screen). A printer provides a 'Hard Copy' output (a permanent physical copy printed on paper).

important_entities.name: Scanner
important_entities.key_fact: Converts Hard Copy to Soft Copy
important_entities.significance: It scans a physical document or photograph (hard copy) and converts it into a digital file (soft copy) stored inside the computer.

important_entities.name: Printer
important_entities.key_fact: Converts Soft Copy to Hard Copy
important_entities.significance: It performs the exact reverse operation of a scanner.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Aspirants frequently confuse audio devices. 
Microphone (Mic) = Input Device (takes your voice INTO the computer).
Speaker = Output Device (pushes audio OUT of the computer).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Is a Touch Screen Input or Output?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A touch screen is a dual-purpose device. It functions as BOTH an Input device (sensing your finger taps) and an Output device (displaying the visual interface).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: If it feeds the brain, it's IN; if it shows the result, it's OUT
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Typing letters feeds the CPU (Input). Printing a page shows the CPU's work (Output).

exam_strategy_tips: The most common question format in Tier-1 exams is 'Find the odd one out', where three input devices and one output device (e.g., Monitor) are listed. Memorize the basic lists thoroughly.
